title.narrative: FJ Institutionalizing the Monitoring of Telecommunications Reform

description.narrative: "The objective is develop the capacity of the new Telecommunications Authority of Fiji to monitor and assess the performance of operators in the newly-liberalized telecommunications sector in their delivery of services to households and businessescomma particularly in rural and remote areas. This activity will not only strengthen oversight of and accountability within the industrycomma but also help to determine the longer-term impact of telecommunications reform on poorer and disadvantaged communities in Fijicomma as well as on the country's business climate and economic opportunities more broadly. By focusing on results monitoring and disseminationcomma this activity will also demonstrate a new accountability approach and mechanism for public institutions in the country. The proposed components are: (1) Advisory assistance and training on the development of a sector performance monitoring framework and instrumentscomma including but not limited to advice on best practice regulationscomma and development of databases on lawscomma regulationscomma licenses and licensingcomma investmentcomma sector revenuescomma population and geographical coverage indicatorscomma quality of service indicatorscomma wholesale and retail pricingcomma and related matters. This entails the development of a robust set of regulations and compliance monitoring mechanisms. (2) Database design and development. Advisory assistance and training to develop an institutional Intranet/portalcomma with selected items (including industry performance and compliance) to be made accessible to the public via an external website. This will contribute to institutional accountabilitycomma transparencycomma and greatly improve consumer awareness. (3) Consultations: a key element of successful and transparent regulation is regular consultation between the regulator and industry. The activity will therefore include an annual consultation mechanismcomma based on a ""report card"" approach. In October 2008 Fiji formally opened up its telecommunications market to competition. This newly-liberalized market offers the prospect of much-improved access to telecommunications infrastructure and servicescomma with wide-ranging economic and social benefits. Ensuring that the sector is effectively monitored and well-regulated so that the market remains competitivecomma services remain affordablecomma are available on an equitable basis and of acceptable quality is therefore essential. Fiji has established a new telecommunications regulatory authority for this purpose. This institution needs the skills and resources to manage the transition from a monopolistic to a competitivecomma multi-operator marketcomma and the tools to measure and demonstrate the impact of the telecommunications sector reform to the broader community."
